ir.name: objective_diff_weight_all_pairs
ir.intuition: Weight each winner/loser pair by the absolute difference in objective values, using lower objective as winner (with tie-breaker on lower log_prob) to correct winner/loser semantics.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    log_prob = feature_cache['log_prob']
    # lower objective is better; tie-break with lower log_prob
    mask = (objective[:, :, None] < objective[:, None, :]) | ((objective[:, :, None] == objective[:, None, :]) & (log_prob[:, :, None] < log_prob[:, None, :]))
    b_idx, i, j = mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    winner_idx = i
    loser_idx = j
    weight = (objective[b_idx, winner_idx] - objective[b_idx, loser_idx]).abs() + 1e-6
    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=weight, meta={'builder': 'objective_diff_weight_all_pairs'})

ir.name: pairwise_pref_cost_gap_stabilized
ir.intuition: Original loss scales the difference of log probabilities by the reciprocal of the absolute cost gap, which can cause numerical instability or extremely large gradients if cost_gap is near zero. This version stabilizes by clamping the denominator to a minimum epsilon (1e-4) to avoid huge scale values, and ensures weight is non-negative as required. This normalization prevents instability and overly large updates while preserving the pairwise preference signal based on cost gap.
ir.pseudocode: clamped_gap = clamp(abs(cost_gap), min=1e-4) scale = 1 / clamped_gap diff = log_prob_l - log_prob_w scaled_diff = diff * weight * scale loss = mean(logsigmoid(scaled_diff))
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    epsilon = 1e-4
    log_prob_w = batch['log_prob_w']
    log_prob_l = batch['log_prob_l']
    weight = batch['weight']
    cost_gap = batch['cost_gap']

    clamped_gap = ops.clamp(ops.abs(cost_gap), min=epsilon)
    scale = 1.0 / clamped_gap
    diff = log_prob_l - log_prob_w
    scaled_diff = diff * weight * scale

    loss = ops.mean(ops.logsigmoid(scaled_diff))
    return loss
